questions.q: Write a 100-word "character entry" for a fictional village elder (not in the text) who would fit seamlessly into the world of "fcLdksgj dh ekVh," using the same narrative voice and descriptive style as the author. Include one specific habit, one physical detail, and one line of dialogue.
questions.a: Criteria for a good answer: (1) Uses the author's sensory, rhythmic prose style (repetition, onomatopoeia, compound words). (2) The elder feels authentic to the village milieu — e.g., a potter, a storyteller, a midwife. (3) Habit is specific and revealing (e.g., "ties his turban with a left-handed knot every morning"). (4) Physical detail is vivid (e.g., "hands cracked like dry riverbed, thumbs stained black from clay"). (5) Dialogue sounds like the text's dialect-inflected Hindi (e.g., "beta, mitti ka ghada toot jaye to phir bhi banta hai, par mann ka ghada toot jaye to..."). A poor answer writes in modern, formal Hindi, gives generic traits ("wise old man"), or imports urban sensibilities. This reveals the student has not internalized the text's linguistic texture.
